answer: The tax collector advertises the tax lien for sale by public auction and issues a tax lien certificate in favor of the winning bidder, recorded in the mortgage records.
quote: the tax collector will advertise for sale by public auction the tax lien and that the tax collector will issue in favor of the winning bidder and record in the mortgage records a tax lien certificate.
note: Louisiana replaced tax sales with tax lien auctions by Acts 2024, No. 774 (and Acts 2025, No. 411), effective 2026-01-01; Const. Art. VII, Sec. 25 was amended by Acts 2024, No. 409, eff. 2026-01-01. Sales before 2026-01-01 follow the law in effect on 2025-12-31 (R.S. 47:2241.1).

answer: The tax collector advertises the tax lien auction on or before May 1 of the year after the taxes were assessed, or as soon as possible after that. Bidding is held on weekdays, opening no earlier than 8:00 a.m. and closing no later than 8:00 p.m.
quote: The tax collector shall advertise for sale by public auction the tax lien on or before May first of the year following the year in which the taxes were assessed, or as soon thereafter as possible. ... The tax lien auction shall be conducted on any weekday, with bidding opening not earlier than 8:00 a.m. and closing no later than 8:00 p.m.

answer: The law allows a tax lien auction to be held online or electronically over several days; bids placed before the auction opens are void.
quote: If a tax lien auction is conducted by using an online or electronic bidding process that is conducted over the course of multiple days, bids may be placed on any day at any time on any tax lien upon which bidding has not closed, provided that all bidding closes on a weekday within the hours prescribed in this Subsection. Any bid received prior to the opening of the auction shall be null and void.

note: State law refers to registered tax lien auction participants but does not set a registration procedure; check the parish tax collector.

answer: The tax collector may require registered participants to pay a deposit of up to $1,000 before the auction. A winner's deposit is applied to the price; other bidders' deposits are returned within 14 days after the auction closes.
quote: The tax collector may require all registered tax lien auction participants to provide a deposit, not to exceed one thousand dollars, prior to the commencement of the tax lien auction. If a deposit is required, the deposit of the winning bidder shall be applied toward the sale price at the time of purchase. A deposit from a nonwinning bidder shall be returned or refunded to the depositor no later than fourteen days after the close of the auction.

answer: The auction price is the face value of the tax lien certificate. Bidders compete on the monthly interest rate, starting from a maximum of 1% per month and bidding down in steps of 0.1%; no bid below 0.7% per month is accepted.
quote: The auction price shall be the face value of the tax lien certificate. ... Subject to a maximum bid of one percent per month, bidders may submit bids reducing the monthly interest rate in increments of one-tenth of one percent or an integral multiple thereof. ... no bid shall be accepted that purports to reduce the rate of monthly interest below seven-tenths of one percent.

answer: The statutory advertisement says the sale is for cash or another payment method the tax collector accepts. The law quoted does not state a payment deadline.
quote: At the auction, I will sell the tax lien to the winning bidder. The sale will be for cash or other payment method acceptable to the tax collector, in legal tender money of the United States.

answer: The clerk of court's recording cost is included in the price paid at the auction and in the face value of the certificate.
quote: The recording cost due to the clerk of court shall be included in the price paid at the tax lien auction and the face value of the tax lien certificate.

answer: Anyone may extinguish the tax lien by paying the termination price to the tax collector until close of business on the 30th day after the last party is served in the certificate holder's enforcement suit.
quote: Until close of business on the thirtieth day following the date on which the last party was served, or the next day that is not a legal holiday if the thirtieth day is a legal holiday, any person may cause the tax lien to be extinguished by delivering the termination price to the tax collector.

answer: After the later of three years from recording the tax lien certificate or six months after the required post-auction notices, a certificate holder may sue to have the delinquent obligation and the lien recognized.
quote: Upon the expiration of the later of three years from recordation of the tax lien certificate, or the tax sale certificate if R.S. 47:2201(B) is applicable, or six months after providing the notices required by R.S. 47:2156, a certificate holder may, by verified petition, institute in a court of competent jurisdiction
note: The winning bidder receives a tax lien certificate, not a deed (R.S. 47:2154(E)); property passes only through the judicial sale in R.S. 47:2267, executed by the sheriff. Louisiana replaced tax sales with tax lien auctions by Acts 2024, No. 774 (and Acts 2025, No. 411), effective 2026-01-01; Const. Art. VII, Sec. 25 was amended by Acts 2024, No. 409, eff. 2026-01-01. Sales before 2026-01-01 follow the law in effect on 2025-12-31 (R.S. 47:2241.1).

answer: A judicial sale to enforce the tax lien ends all interests in the property, except rights created by certain written instruments listed in the statute that were filed before the tax lien certificate was recorded.
quote: a judicial sale pursuant to R.S. 47:2267 shall terminate all interests in the immovable property. B. The rights and obligations established or created by the following written instruments affecting immovable property shall not be terminated pursuant to this Chapter to the extent the interests remain effective against third persons and are filed with the appropriate recorder prior to the recordation of the tax lien certificate:

answer: If no one bids, the tax collector issues and records the tax lien certificate in favor of the political subdivision.
quote: If there is no bidder, the tax collector shall issue and record the tax lien certificate in favor of the political subdivision.

note: No statutory buyer-diligence instruction was found in the sections read (R.S. 47:2121 et seq.).

answer: At the tax lien auction the winning bidder receives a tax lien certificate, recorded in the parish mortgage records, which is prima facie evidence of the lien and its assignment to the holder.
quote: No later than thirty days after conclusion of the tax lien auction, the tax collector shall issue and file in the mortgage records of the parish in which the property is situated a tax lien certificate in favor of the winning bidder. ... The tax lien certificate shall be prima facie evidence of the validity of the tax lien and the assignment to the person named thereon.
note: Louisiana replaced tax sales with tax lien auctions by Acts 2024, No. 774 (and Acts 2025, No. 411), effective 2026-01-01; Const. Art. VII, Sec. 25 was amended by Acts 2024, No. 409, eff. 2026-01-01. Sales before 2026-01-01 follow the law in effect on 2025-12-31 (R.S. 47:2241.1).

answer: Bidding is on the monthly interest rate that will accrue on the certificate's face value; the lowest rate wins, and a tie goes to the bidder who bid first.
quote: The subject of the competitive bidding shall be the monthly rate at which interest will accrue on the face value of the tax lien certificate following its issuance. ... The bid that requires the assessment of interest at the lowest rate shall be declared the winner. If multiple bidders submit the same lowest bid, the winner shall be the first in time to submit the bid.

answer: Interest accrues on the certificate's face value at the monthly rate set by the winning bid, or at 1% per month when the political subdivision holds the certificate, in both cases without compounding.
quote: Upon the issuance of a tax lien certificate, interest shall accrue on the face value of the tax lien certificate at the monthly rate established by the winning bid at the tax lien auction. If the tax lien certificate is issued in favor of the political subdivision, interest shall accrue on the face value of the tax lien certificate at the rate of one percent per month. In both cases, interest shall be calculated on a noncompounding basis.

answer: The taxes, interest, penalties and costs may be paid at any time until thirty days after service of a petition to enforce the tax lien.
quote: the statutory impositions, together with interest, penalties, and costs, may be paid at any time prior to the expiration of thirty days after service of a petition to enforce the tax lien.

answer: A judgment for the certificate holder in an enforcement action under R.S. 47:2266.1 is executed by a writ of fieri facias under the Code of Civil Procedure (a judicial sale).
quote: a judgment rendered in favor of the tax lien certificate holder in an action brought pursuant to R.S. 47:2266.1 shall be executed by a writ of fieri facias in accordance with the provisions of Title II of Book IV of the Code of Civil Procedure

answer: An action to enforce the tax lien must be brought within seven years from recording the tax lien certificate in the parish mortgage records; after that the tax lien is extinguished.
quote: An action to enforce the tax lien pursuant to R.S. 47:2266.1 shall be brought no later than seven years from the date that the tax lien certificate is recorded in the mortgage records of the parish in which the property is located. Upon the expiration of this time period, the tax lien shall be extinguished

answer: Adjudicated property is property whose tax sale title a political subdivision acquired under R.S. 47:2196 before January 1, 2026.
quote: "Adjudicated property" means property of which tax sale title is acquired by a political subdivision pursuant to R.S. 47:2196 prior to January 1, 2026.
note: Sales authority: R.S. 47:2201(A)(1). Louisiana replaced tax sales with tax lien auctions by Acts 2024, No. 774 (and Acts 2025, No. 411), effective 2026-01-01; Const. Art. VII, Sec. 25 was amended by Acts 2024, No. 409, eff. 2026-01-01. Sales before 2026-01-01 follow the law in effect on 2025-12-31 (R.S. 47:2241.1).

answer: Any person may start the public sale of adjudicated property by making a written request to the political subdivision and depositing the amount it sets to cover the sale's expenses, including advertising and appraisals.
quote: any person may initiate the public sale of adjudicated property or property subject to a tax lien certificate held by a political subdivision by making a written request to the political subdivision and depositing an amount determined by the political subdivision to be sufficient to cover the expenses of the sale, including advertising, appraisals, and other costs associated with the sale.

answer: The political subdivision may sell to the highest bidder without a minimum bid or appraisal. If it sets a dollar minimum bid, that minimum must be at least the statutory impositions, governmental liens and costs of sale.
quote: The governing authority of each political subdivision may elect to sell adjudicated property at a public sale to the highest bidder without setting a minimum bid or requiring an appraisal. (2) If the governing authority elects to set a dollar amount as a minimum bid for the public sale of adjudicated property, the minimum bid shall be no less than the total amount of statutory impositions, governmental liens, and costs of sale.

answer: The buyer files the act of sale or donation and pays all filing fees.
quote: A transferee of immovable property in accordance with this Subpart shall be responsible for filing the act of sale or donation and payment of all filing fees.

note: State law sets no form; the political subdivision's ordinance governs (R.S. 47:2201, 2204).
No statewide payment rule found; the political subdivision's ordinance governs.

answer: The political subdivision's only warranty is against eviction resulting from its own prior sale; otherwise the sale is without any warranty, even as to return or reduction of the price.
quote: The only warranty owed by the political subdivision shall be a warranty against eviction resulting from a prior alienation by the political subdivision. Otherwise, all sales and donations shall be without warranty, either expressed or implied, even as to return or reduction of the purchase price

note: No statutory time limit on how long adjudicated property stays available was found.

answer: Sales of adjudicated property are handled through the Office of the Parish Attorney, telephone (225) 389-3114.
quote: Abandoned adjudicated property sales for the Parish are handled through the Office of the Parish Attorney. Questions concerning the sale process and procedures should be addressed to that office, telephone number (225) 389-3114
source_title: MEMORANDUM - Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division (purchase of adjudicated property)

answer: First confirm that the property was adjudicated and is still adjudicated to the City-Parish (the City-Parish keeps no list of adjudicated properties), then call the Parish Attorney's Office to confirm it is still available.
quote: you must first determine that the property in which you are interested has in fact been adjudicated, and is still adjudicated, to the City-Parish. The City-Parish does not maintain a roster/ list/ database of properties that are adjudicated. ... you must call the Parish Attorney's Office so that someone in our office can confirm that the property is still currently available
source_title: MEMORANDUM - Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division (purchase of adjudicated property)
note: The Parish Attorney's own page also links an open-data list and CivicSource; the memorandum states the City-Parish keeps no list.

answer: Offers need not equal the appraised value or the taxes and public liens; the Metropolitan Council considers those amounts when deciding whether to accept or reject the offer.
quote: Offers do not have to equal or exceed either the appraised value or the amount of taxes and public liens. However, these amounts will be considered by the Metropolitan Council at a regularly scheduled meeting in which it will be determined whether to accept or reject your offer.
source_title: MEMORANDUM - Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division (purchase of adjudicated property)

answer: Advanced costs are at least $500 per property, and some properties have additional costs; this fee is not part of the sale price. The buyer also pays all fees and expenses to record the sale documents.
quote: This amount will be a MINIMUM of $500. However, each individual property may have additional amounts due for costs. ... This fee is not part of the sales price that is ultimately paid to buy the property. ... You are responsible for all fees and expense to record these documents.
source_title: MEMORANDUM - Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division (purchase of adjudicated property)

answer: To open a file: a completed 'Request to Purchase Adjudicated Property' form, the two-page tax print and current tax bill from the Sheriff, and a certified check or money order for advanced costs for each property, among other items.
quote: A completed "Request to Purchase Adjudicated Property" form . ... A copy of the two page tax print and the current tax bill for that particular property. You will obtain this from the East Baton Rouge Parish Sheriff. ... A certified check or money order for advanced costs for each piece of property you open a file on.
source_title: MEMORANDUM - Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division (purchase of adjudicated property)

answer: Advanced costs are paid by certified check or money order payable to the City of Baton Rouge (no personal checks or cash). The sale price is paid with certified funds at the closing.
quote: NO PERSONAL CHECKS OR CASH can be accepted. Checks must be made payable to the "City of Baton Rouge." ... Please note that you will be required to pay the sales price with certified funds at the time of the sale.
source_title: MEMORANDUM - Office of the Parish Attorney, Property Division (purchase of adjudicated property)
